content.text: No minimum commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction exists anywhere in the agreement. Compensation is purely time-and-materials for ordered work, which matches our preferred position.

input.quote: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction binding Clear Capital. Section 3(a) compensates Contractor on a time-and-materials basis solely as set forth in each Statement of Work, and Section 1(a) engages Contractor "on a task by task basis," so fees are payable only for services actually ordered and performed — our preferred position. A targeted regex search for "minimum", "shortfall", "take-or-pay", "retainer", "guarantee", "commit", "volume" and "non-refundable" returned only unrelated hits (exclusive-property and entire-agreement language in Sections 4 and 7). Section 6(b) caps amounts on termination at "all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned ... through the effective date of such termination," which is a true-up rather than a penalty, and no early-termination or cancellation fee appears. Section 6(a)'s limit on convenience termination while an SOW is outstanding is a term/exit-right issue rather than a purchase commitment, and it creates no obligation to buy a minimum quantity. Residual risk sits in individual Statements of Work, which are not before us; helpfully, Section 1(a) provides that this Agreement controls over conflicting SOW provisions. No redline required.
